what: Real petty-cash vouchers of one small Taiwanese company, used with the owner's consent. Only aggregate counts are published: no images, no company name, no tax ID, no per-voucher values.
answer_key: 4 labelers read the page images only (no ledger, no OCR, no Ledger Room); frozen (sha256 prefix fcff2ca60a393f7d) before any Ledger Room read. Kept outside git.

by_kind_9B.fields_scored: invoice_no, date, seller_ubn, total, net, tax (as eval/real_photo_eval.py TW_FIELDS); a utility bill's printed invoice number is the previous period's e-invoice

old_ledger_vs_ledger_room.what: The company's own ledger rows for its invoices were typed by a general cloud chat AI and checked once by the owner. 113 of the 121 invoices could be paired with a ledger row (106 by exact invoice number, 7 by a near-miss number with the same date or amount). Compared on the three fields that ledger keeps: invoice number, date, total.
old_ledger_vs_ledger_room.note: Not a person-versus-machine race: the old ledger is one way a small company actually kept its books. On all six scored fields the 9B let 1 of the 113 through (a seller tax ID), which the old ledger does not record.

after_fix_utility_routing.what: A recognised utility bill is not booked from paper: its input tax comes from the utility's e-invoice on the MOF platform, the bill is kept as payment proof. It is neither held nor exported.
